answer: At a settlement wharf, an agent may bid only after locking a 60-day, non-transferable bond of 200 units under a hardware-bound signing quill. Weight then accrues solely with uninterrupted lock age, the way mineral crust thickens inside a karst conduit: a one-year lock outranks a hundred accounts opened this week, and cloning the quill collapses every alias onto one weight. To field 1,000 credible identities, an attacker must immobilize 200,000 units for months and buy 1,000 distinct secure elements, forfeiting that capital's use the entire time.
